svg.title: Shared-interleaver Hankel cell
svg.desc: Three unfolded paths show separate operations of the same cell. Forward runs left to right: A input, shared interleaver outward, stored weights and reference, Kerr FWM, B-family selection, G1, same interleaver returning, the B-band two-copy interferometer, gate, G2, B output. Adjoint runs right to left: a B residual advanced by 63δ enters the B copier then the shared interleaver, mixes with the same weights and reference, and returns in A through G1, the interleaver, gate and G2. Both passes use a co-propagating guide in its physical forward direction. The write sends saved A and coded B concurrently through the interleaver, mixes them with R, selects the full 127-tooth coefficient family, and injects the selected slot into the circulating weights. The old weight read tap is off during the write. A separate port initializes the loop. The long TTT memory returns all 127 weight teeth through one in-line section of dispersion-compensating fiber. Repeated interleaver, copier, guide, selector and amplifier symbols denote scheduled reuse. Arrows show propagation. Colored lines identify the indicated signal band; pump multiplexers admit multiple bands. Optical path lengths and couplers are schematic. Gate starts are 63P+T forward and 63P adjoint; the B residual is advanced by 63δ, with P=45 ps, T=20 ps and δ=T/64. G1 is +10 dB; G2 is +29.8 dB at identity calibration and +31.07 dB for the trained-matrix budget. Logical labels omit the fixed spectral phase and field-conjugation convention. Amplifier loading, backprop accuracy and memory retention are separate design questions.

g.title: Folded optical path and one stage of the shared interleaver
g.desc: Forward read: band A travels outward through the shared interleaver and the co-propagating Kerr guide. The selected B idler is amplified and routed back through the same interleaver. In stage b both bands share the long delay, and the entire B band takes an additional delay before rejoining A.
